title: Philips Hue 2700K White A67 High Brightness 100W (1600 Lumens) E27 or B22 Smart Bulb $22.95 Delivered + More @ Philips Hue
body:
Deal: Philips Hue 2700K White A67 High Brightness 100W (1600 Lumens) E27 or B22 Smart Bulb $22.95 Delivered + More @ Philips Hue

[BestTechAdvisor] If anyone wants RGB, TP-Link Tapo are on sale for $25 for a 2-Pack. ATL was $22. IKEA also has their RGB Smart Bulb available for $20 for a 1-Pack, or $25 for bulb + remote switch kit. IKEA reviews don't seem to match TP-Link or Philips though.
[Wombatstew] Reminder for anyone concerned with cost of larger Hue systems - IKEA globes can be added to Hue bridge. Flick them off and on 7 times and they will reset and show up in the add device list. I've had 1 instance where a light just wouldn't recognise and I needed to use 'Hue Lights' app (not the regular 'Hue' app) which essentially allows force identification on the network.
[BestTechAdvisor] Hue is the gold standard, but Tapo is half the price. Both are reviewed well on Amazon (4.5 vs 4.7). If money is no object, choose Philips. If you don't want to get locked into Philips' expensive ecosystem once this deal is over, choose TP-Link.
[Zeee] Phillips so expensive. Not sure why? Even 22 for a bulb, sounds too much for me
[Graffin] The HUE ecosystem is really expensive, but it's the best (as others have said).
I've had others (Lifx, Mirabella Genio, TP Link, etc) - and anything that connects to wifi (particularly devices that can only connect to the 2.4GHz band) often randomly disconnect, whereas HUE keeps on working even if the internet is down.
[BestTechAdvisor] @Graffin: To fix the 2.4GHz issue, it's usually a good idea to create a network only for your IoT devices that is 2.4GHz only. Even most entry level routers can do this via a Guest Network.
[Graffin] @BestTechAdvisor: I’ve tried that, and also upgrading to a TP Link Archer AX6000 router and it’s still a slight issue with cheap brand smart lights… I guess having 59 devices connected doesn’t help things too!
[pitufon] Take the cheap hue. You don't get locked in anywhere. I have about 15+ hue devices mixed with ikea and nanoleaf and merros. No issues there.
[A 1] Agreed, at this price go the hue. They work really well for me, my failure rate has been ~4% over 5 years which I think is decent (considering some are in sealed fittings (not recommended by Philips due to heat)).
Cheers OP!
[infringement payer] Any idea when the Hue Essentials line up (e.g essentials white) will come out in Australia?
[Nom] Why would they need to be available in Australia specifically ? They're readily available on Amazon.com.au right now from other 240v countries like the UK and Germany.
[Westpac] hmm should i buy from amazon or from philips… 20% vs free returns any thoughts?
[oatmatcha] Choose your OzBargain adventure: maximise savings, or buy now think later.
[NigelTufnel] Not a huge fan of being locked to 2700K in a smart light.
[A 1] The Hue "Ambience" (adjustable colour temperature) are also on clearance, not quite as cheap but still significantly discounted.
[Hargain Bunter] Thanks paid a bit extra for the white ambiance ($34.95) haven’t seen them on sale for a long time!
[Davbar24] The last time I got high brightness ones the bulbs were larger so didn't fit some of my light fittings with covers. Was a few years ago. Anyone know if the size has changed at all?
[A 1] If you're talking 1100 lumens vs 1600, still the same issue, look at the images of the products closely and you can see the extra height of the 1600 lumen globes. It does cause issues unfortunately, I only use the 1600s in open fittings.
[mblack77] Why is the image for the deal a colour bulb but the product is white?
[hamza23] It just grabs whatever image is on the linked page. I'll manually update it.
[Averell] I'm looking for smart lights to be installed as recessed downlights on a sloped ceiling. I tried to search IKEA/Hue/Tapo, and couldn't find any suitable product. What are options for sloped ceiling? I found some fittings with a gimbal, which take either MR16 or GU10 bulbs, but no plug-and-play options.
Thanks
